---
title: Slurm arrays
description: Submit, throttle, and inspect HTSeq jobs on a Slurm cluster.
---

When the same counting command must run across many BAM files, a Slurm array
keeps the submission together without combining the samples into one task.

Each array task reads one generated TSV row. This avoids shell parsing of paths
and sample identifiers.

```bash
htseq-count-cluster run \
  --scheduler slurm \
  --infile samples.csv \
  --gtf genes.gtf \
  --outpath counts \
  --partition short \
  --account my-allocation \
  --memory 4G \
  --time 02:00:00 \
  --max-concurrent 8
```

Here, `--max-concurrent 8` allows at most eight tasks to run at once. Adjust that
limit to match the cluster policy and your allocation.

The CPU count is a scheduler request. `htseq-count` remains a single-process
command.

## Check status once

```bash
htseq-count-cluster status --scheduler slurm 12345678
```

This checks the job once rather than polling. The command queries:

1. `squeue` for a current job;
2. `sacct` after the job leaves the queue.

The reported state is `Queued`, `Running`, `Finished`, `Failed`, or `Unknown`.

## Inspect failures

Start with the failed array task's log. The retained submission files serve
different purposes:

- `logs/` contains files named with the job and task identifiers.
- The manifest records the input assigned to each task.
- `run-array.sh` records the task command.
